DURR-FULL:v6p502/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p502/r4.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v6p502/r4.claim: When a Kharijite called out a warning about shirk while Ali prayed, Ali answered with the command to be patient because God’s promise is true.
DURR-FULL:v6p502/r4.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه أن رجلا من الخوارج ناداه وهو في صلاة الفجر فقال {ولقد أوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك

ZAJJAJ:v4p191/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p191/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p191/r3.claim: God's promise of victory over the enemy and establishment of Islam is true; doubters should not provoke the Prophet from his religion.
ZAJJAJ:v4p191/r3.anchor: أي إن ما وعدك الله من النصر على عدوك حق، وإظهار دين الإسلام حق.

STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r14.claim: The sūrah closes by recalling that disbelievers’ hearts are sealed and urging steadfastness when facing them.
STUDYQURAN:30:intro/r14.anchor: The sūrah concludes with a reminder that their hearts are sealed (v. 59) and that one must thus remain steadfast when confronted by them (v. 60).

BURSEVI:v7p45/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to endure his opponents' verbal and physical abuse; God's promise to give him victory and manifest his religion is true and certain to be fulfilled.
BURSEVI:v7p45/r1.anchor: {فاصبر} يا محمد على أذاهم قولا وفعلا

BURSEVI:v7p45/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45/r2.claim: Yastakhiffannak means not to let them unsettle or distress him.
BURSEVI:v7p45/r2.anchor: لا يحملنك على الخفة والقلق جزعا

BURSEVI:v7p45/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v7p45/r3.claim: The phrase means do not let their doubts agitate you or dislodge you from your belief.
BURSEVI:v7p45/r3.anchor: لا يزعجنك ولا يزيلنك عن اعتقادك

BURSEVI:v7p45/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45/r4.claim: The unbelievers lack certainty, deny the signs, and use false accusations such as calling the messengers liars; such behavior is expected from doubters astray.
BURSEVI:v7p45/r4.anchor: فإنهم شاكّون ضالون ولا يستبدع منهم أمثال ذلك

BURSEVI:v7p45/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45/r5.claim: Although the wording appears to forbid the unbelievers from undermining the Prophet, it indirectly forbids him from being affected by their contempt.
BURSEVI:v7p45/r5.anchor: فظاهر النظم الكريم وإن كان نهيا للكفرة عن استخفافه عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v7p45/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45/r6.claim: After Abu Talib died, Quraysh intensified their abuse; one fool threw dust on the Prophet's head, and when his daughter wept while wiping it away he reassured her that God would protect him. The Companions also endured abuse and ultimately prevailed.
BURSEVI:v7p45/r6.anchor: روي أنه لما مات أبو طالب عم النبي عليه السلام بالغ قريش في الأذى

BURSEVI:v7p45/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r7.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v7p45/r7.claim: His verse urges steadfastness in love because this path does not go unrewarded.
BURSEVI:v7p45/r7.anchor: دلادر عاشقى ثابت قدم باش كه دراين ره نباشد كار بى اجر

BURSEVI:v7p45/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r8.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v7p45/r8.claim: For a sincere seeker, patience means disciplining the self away from familiar desires, guarding the heart from ego traits, and helping the spirit give up its existence to receive divine generosity.
BURSEVI:v7p45/r8.anchor: يشير إلى الطالب الصادق فاصبر على مقاساة شدائد فطام النفس

BURSEVI:v7p45/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45/r9.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v7p45/r9.claim: God's true promise to the seeker is expressed as: whoever seeks Me will find Me.

BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r1.claim: The verse also warns against idle people who belittle truth-seekers as ignorant; even those with inherited faith may lack certainty and try to block seekers with mockery and denial.
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r1.anchor: يشير به إلى استخفاف أهل البطالة واستجهالهم أهل الحق وطلبه

BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r2.claim: Such critics deny that seeking God is obligatory and scorn those who leave worldly life, family, and children for the quest.
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r2.anchor: لأنهم لا يوقنون بوجوب طلب الحق تعالى

BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r3.claim: A seeker first needs outward detachment, then inward separation of the heart from attachment to happiness in either world; by these two steps people reach unity.
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r3.anchor: ويجب على طالبي الحق أولا التجريد

BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r4.claim: The cited saying summarizes the path as two steps followed by arrival.
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r4.anchor: كما قال بعضهم خطوتان وقد وصلت

BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r5.speaker: العطار
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r5.claim: His poem compares annihilation of the self to a clod falling into the sea: once the clod loses its separate self, only the sea remains; while it insists on itself, it cannot find union.
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r5.anchor: مكرسنك وكلوخى بود درراه بدريايى در افتادند ناكاه

BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r6.claim: The Mathnawi story of a grammarian and a boatman teaches that grammar cannot save the scholar from drowning; self-effacement is needed, and the sea carries the dead while the living may drown.
BURSEVI:v7p45#2/r6.anchor: ليك اندم كرد خاموش از جواب باد كشتى را بكردابى فكند

SULAMI:v2p128#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p128#4/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p128#4/r2.claim: Confidence in the generous reward promised to the patient makes hardships easy to endure and removes the pain of remaining in them.
SULAMI:v2p128#4/r2.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : من تحقق بما وعد الله الصابرين من جميل الثواب وحسن العطاء

SULAMI:v2p128#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p128#4/r3.speaker: الحارث المحاسبي
SULAMI:v2p128#4/r3.claim: Patience means exposing oneself to the arrows of affliction.
SULAMI:v2p128#4/r3.anchor: سمعت حارث المحاسبي - رحمة الله عليه - يقول : الصبر التهدف لسهام البلاء

NAHHAS:v3p279/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p279/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p279/r6.claim: The command to endure is jussive, reinforced by heavy nūn and therefore built on fatḥa; الذين لا يوقنون is nominative.
NAHHAS:v3p279/r6.anchor: في موضع جزم بالنهي فأكد بالنون الثقيلة فبني على الفتح

NAHHAS:v3p279/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p279/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p279/r7.claim: Some Arabs use الذون in nominative instead of الذين.
NAHHAS:v3p279/r7.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول الذون في موضع الرفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r3.claim: Patience follows the reminder that they will not believe; its omitted object is their obstinacy, and God's certain promise reassures the Prophet of retribution and victory.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r4.claim: الحق is the substantive of حق يحق, meaning established and certain without exaggeration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r4.anchor: الثابت الذي لا ريب فيه ولا مبالغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r5.claim: استخف means making light of something and is intensified; here it means not letting disbelievers provoke him into abandoning patience, with lightness figuratively expressing panic or visible anger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p134/r5.anchor: مبالغة في جعله خفيفا فالسين والتاء للتقوية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is told to be patient, trust God's true promise, and remain unmoved by people who lack certainty or insight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r6.anchor: ثم أمر نبيه بالصبر وقوى نفسه لتحقيق الوعد ونهاه عن الاهتزاز لكلامهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r7.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق ويعقوب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r7.claim: They read yastaḥiqqannaka from istihqāq; the majority read yastakhiffannaka from istikhfāf, and the two readers also report a silent nūn in that form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ويعقوب «يستحقنك» بحاء غير معجمة وقاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r8.claim: While Ali prayed dawn prayer, a Kharijite shouted a verse accusing him of shirk; Ali recognized the insinuation and answered by reciting the command to be patient.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p344#2/r8.anchor: وروي أن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه كان في صلاة الفجر فناداه رجل من الخوارج بأعلى صوته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r1.claim: The promise that God will grant the Prophet victory and prevail him over his enemy is true.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r1.anchor: فاصبر إن وعد الله بنصرك وإظهارك على عدوك حق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r2.speaker: يعقوب إلا روحا وزيدا
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r2.claim: Yaʿqūb, except for Rawḥ and Zayd, reads “yستخفنك” with the nūn unvowelled.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r2.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب إلا روحا وزيدا يستخفنك بسكون النون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r3.claim: The warning means the unbelievers must not unsettle the Prophet from his religion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج لا يستفزنك عن دينك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r4.claim: Those without certainty are astray and doubtful.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r5.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that they have no certainty about resurrection and recompense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r5.anchor: وقال غيره لا يوقنون بالبعث والجزاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r6.claim: Some exegetes claim this verse has been abrogated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p313/r6.anchor: وزعم بعض المفسرين أن هذه الآية منسوخة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328#2/r1.claim: God gave people many examples to clarify truth, yet disbelievers call any sign false or magic, as they did the moon's splitting; even every sign would not move those condemned to disbelief, as in 10:96–97.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328#2/r1.anchor: لو رأوا أي آية كانت، سواء كانت باقتراحهم أو غيره، لا يؤمنون بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328#2/r2.claim: The Prophet should patiently endure opposition, trusting God's promised victory and good end, and stand firm because truth alone is guidance rather than being unsettled by unbelievers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p328#2/r2.anchor: بل اثبت على ما بعثك الله به، فإنه الحق الذي لا مرية فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p329/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p329/r1.speaker: صحابي من أصحاب النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p329/r1.claim: When the Prophet stumbled while reciting Sūrat al-Rūm in dawn prayer, he said poor ablution by some worshipers had confused the Quran and instructed those praying with him to perform ablution well; Ibn Kathīr grades the chain and text ḥasan and infers the follower's prayer is connected to the imam's.

JISHUMI:v8p5639/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5639/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5639/r5.claim: Istikhfāf is seeking lightness; to make a people light is to prompt them to act hastily, and being overcome by delight removes good judgment.
JISHUMI:v8p5639/r5.anchor: والاستخفاف: طلب الخفة، واستخف قومه: حملهم على الخفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r1.claim: The address to the Prophet promises either God's support and victory or His vengeance on the Prophet's enemies.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r1.anchor: هذا خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : أن وعد الله في نصرك وتأييدك حق

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r2.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r2.claim: He glosses ولا يستخفنك as do not make you hurry.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r3.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r3.claim: He glosses it as do not provoke you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r3.anchor: لا يستفزنك , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r4.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r4.claim: He glosses it as do not draw you down from your position.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r5.claim: Those who lack certainty may be understood as unbelievers or as people who deny resurrection and recompense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r5.anchor: لا يؤمنون . الثاني : لا يصدقون بالبعث والجزاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r6.claim: During dawn prayer, a Kharijite recited the warning about shirk; Ali replied with the command to be patient and not be unsettled by those without certainty.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p324/r6.anchor: روى سعيد عن قتادة أن رجلا من الخوارج قال لعلي كرم الله وجهه وهو خلفه في صلاة الصبح

MUQATIL:30:58-60/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:30:58-60/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:30:58-60/r3.claim: After al-Nadr b. al-Harith demanded immediate punishment, God tells Muhammad not to be provoked by the unconvinced; Badr killed al-Nadr, ʿAli beheaded him, and the dead are displayed to the Fire morning and evening.
MUQATIL:30:58-60/r3.anchor: هذا قول النضر بن الحارث القرشى من بنى عبدالدار بن قصى، فأنزل الله تعالى:

NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r1.claim: Be patient with their harm and hostility; God's promised victory over enemies and the triumph of Islam over every religion must come to pass.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ فاصبر ﴾ على أذاهم أو عداوتهم ﴿ إن وعد الله ﴾ بنصرتك على أعدائك وإظهار دين الإسلام على كل دين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r2.claim: Do not let unbelievers rush you into asking for their punishment, or agitate and distress you through what they say and do; their doubt makes such behavior unsurprising.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r2.anchor: لا يحملنك هؤلاء الذين لا يوقنون بالآخرة على الخفة والعجلة فى الدعاء عليهم بالعذاب أو لا يحملنك على الخفة والقلق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r3.speaker: يعقوب
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the final nūn with sukūn in ولا يستخفنك.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p279#5/r3.anchor: ولا يستخفنك بسكون النون عن يعقوب

QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r4.claim: The Prophet is told to endure their abuse because God's promise to grant victory is true.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r4.anchor: أي اصبر على أذاهم فإن الله ينصرك

QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r5.claim: Istakhiffannaka means do not let those without certainty provoke you away from your religion; they try to make someone foolish enough to follow error.

QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r6.claim: Some identify those without certainty as al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith; although addressed to the Prophet, the warning is intended for his community.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r6.anchor: قيل: هو النضر بن الحارث. والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد أمته

QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r7.claim: The prohibition is jussive and emphasized by the heavy nūn, so its form is built on fatḥ; alladhīna is nominative, with اللذون another Arab nominative form.
QURTUBI-FULL:30:58-60/r7.anchor: أكد بالنون الثقيلة فبني على الفتح

SAMIN-DURR:30:60/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:30:60/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:30:60/r1.claim: The common reading derives يستخفنك from استخفاف; Yaqub and Ibn Abi Ishaq read استحقاق with ح and ق, while Ibn Abi Abla and Yaqub lighten the emphatic ن.
SAMIN-DURR:30:60/r1.anchor: العامة من الاستخفاف بخاء معجمة وفاء. ويعقوب وابن أبي إسحاق بحاء مهملة وقاف

SAMIN-DURR:30:60/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:30:60/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:30:60/r2.claim: The prohibition uses the idiom لا أرينك ههنا.
SAMIN-DURR:30:60/r2.anchor: والنهي من باب قولهم " لا أرينك ههنا

RAZI-FULL:v25p121#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p121#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p121#2/r2.claim: The command to be patient consoles Muhammad: the truth of God’s promise means the Prophet’s truthfulness will become clear.
RAZI-FULL:v25p121#2/r2.anchor: بقوله : { فاصبر إن وعد الله حق } أي أن صدقك يبين

RAZI-FULL:v25p121#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p121#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p121#2/r3.claim: “Do not let the uncertain unsettle you” requires continued invitation to faith; silence would let unbelievers claim the Prophet has changed his position and lacks firmness.
RAZI-FULL:v25p121#2/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى وجوب مداومة النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام على الدعاء إلى الإيمان فإنه لو سكت لقال الكافر إنه متقلب الرأي

STUDYQURAN:30:60/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r1.claim: The promise’s truth echoes 30:6 and is cross-referenced with 4:122, 10:4 and 10:55, 18:21, 28:13, 31:33, 35:5, 40:55 and 40:77, 45:32, and 46:17.
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r1.anchor: That God’s Promise is indeed true (cf. 4:122; 10:4, 55; 18:21

STUDYQURAN:30:60/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r2.speaker: IJ, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r2.claim: One interpretation is that God promises to aid the Prophet and make him prevail.
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r2.anchor: Here it is understood as a reference to God’s Promise to aid the Prophet, to make him prevail (IJ, Ṭ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:30:60/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that God promises to make the Prophet’s veracity clear.
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r3.anchor: and to render his veracity clear (R).

STUDYQURAN:30:60/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r4.speaker: IJ, Q
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r4.claim: The warning about disbelievers’ uncertainty can mean they must not make one restive about one’s religion.
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r4.anchor: not let them make one restive regarding one’s own religion (IJ, Q).

STUDYQURAN:30:60/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r5.claim: Though grammatically addressed to one person, the command is understood as addressing the Prophet’s community as a whole.
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r5.anchor: it is understood as having been addressed to the Prophet’s community as a whole (Q)

STUDYQURAN:30:60/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r6.claim: The verb yastakhiff, translated as disquiet, can mean inducing levity or rushing someone so that they become unsteady.
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r6.anchor: Disquiet translates yastakhiff, which can also mean to induce another to levity or to force another to do something in a hurry and so become unsteady.

STUDYQURAN:30:60/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r7.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r7.claim: A further interpretation is that the verb means making someone heedless or ignorant, leading them into error and transgression.
STUDYQURAN:30:60/r7.anchor: It is also understood to mean making another heedless or ignorant, so that the person then falls into error and transgression (Q).

TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r1.claim: Muhammad must bear his opponents' abuse and deliver God's message, trusting God's true promise of victory, triumph, and establishment for him and his followers in the land.
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {فاصبر إن وعد الله حق، ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون} [الروم: 60] قال: قال رجل من الخوارج

TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r2.claim: Unbelievers who deny resurrection must not shake Muhammad's judgment or deter him from carrying out God's command to deliver the message.
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r2.anchor: ولا يستخفن حلمك ورأيك هؤلاء المشركون بالله

TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r3.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r3.claim: When a Kharijite recited the warning that associating partners would void Muhammad's deeds, Ali answered during prayer with this command to be patient and unshaken; Qatada also transmits the episode.
TAB-FULL:v18p529#2/r3.anchor: عن علي بن ربيعة، أن رجلا من الخوارج قرأ خلف علي

TABATABAI:30:56-60/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:56-60/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:56-60/r8.claim: Muhammad is told to endure their taunts because God's promise of victory is true, as also stated in 30:47; the surah begins and ends with the promise of help.
TABATABAI:30:56-60/r8.anchor: فاصبر على ما يواجهونك به من قولهم { إن أنتم إلا مبطلون } وسائر تهكماتهم، إن وعد الله أنه ينصرك حق

TABATABAI:30:56-60/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:30:56-60/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:30:56-60/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the alternative that patience is urged because disbelievers deny the clear signs and distress the Prophet; the promise at both ends of the surah is victory.
TABATABAI:30:56-60/r9.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن المعنى لا يوقنون بما تتلو عليهم من الآيات البينات بتكذيبهم لها وإيذائهم لك بأباطيلهم، ليس بشيء

TABRISI:30:56-60/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:56-60/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:30:56-60/r11.claim: Muhammad must patiently endure the disbelievers' harm: God's promise of punishment for enemies and support for him and the religion is true.
TABRISI:30:56-60/r11.anchor: بالعذاب والتنكيل لأعدائك والنصر والتأييد لك ولدينك

TABRISI:30:56-60/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:30:56-60/r12.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:30:56-60/r12.claim: Do not let doubters agitate you or provoke haste through anger, making you violate God's command to be patient and gentle.
TABRISI:30:56-60/r12.anchor: لا يحملنك كفر هؤلاء على الخفة والعجلة لشدة الغضب عليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r1.claim: After reporting that their hearts are sealed, God tells the Prophet to be patient until victory: the promise to establish his religion and prevail over his enemy is true.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r1.anchor: أمر نبيه -صلى الله عليه وسلم- بالصبر إلى وقت النصر فقال: {فاصبر إن وعد الله حق ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq glosses the warning as not letting the unbelievers provoke the Prophet away from his religion; they are astray and doubtful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r2.anchor: أبو إسحاق: أي: لا يستفزونك عن دينك {الذين لا يوقنون} أي: هم ضالون شاكون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r3.claim: Al-Azharī says istakhaffa can mean treating someone as foolish and leading him to follow error; here the opponents must not unsettle the Prophet’s judgment and forbearance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r3.anchor: استخف فلان فلانا إذا استجهله فحمله على اتباعه في غيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies those who lack certainty as those who do not believe what the Prophet brought.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r4.anchor: ابن عباس: {الذين لا يوقنون} ما جئت به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r5.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r5.claim: Muqātil says they do not believe punishment will descend on them in this world; these were the people punished at Badr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r5.anchor: مقاتل: لا يوقنون بنزول العذاب عليهم في الدنيا؛ وهم الذين عذبهم الله ببدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p87#3/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that they do not believe in resurrection and judgment.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:59-60/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:59-60/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:59-60/r2.claim: Muhammad must be patient because God’s promise of victory and empowerment is true; doubting disbelievers must not unsettle him or make him abandon religion.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:30:59-60/r2.anchor: في نصرك وتمكينك { حق ولا يستخفنك } لا يستفزنك عن دينك

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p667/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p667/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p667/r4.claim: Muhammad should be patient because God truly promised victory over polytheists and the triumph of his religion; he must not be provoked or follow their call to abandon it.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p667/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p667/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p667/r5.claim: Those lacking certainty are polytheists urging the Prophet to leave his religion.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p667/r5.anchor: ما يدعونك إليه من ترك دينك

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r3.claim: The surah closes by urging patience and trust in God against deniers; the Prophet and believers are comforted and told to remain steadfast despite their pressure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r3.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem’e ve onun şahsında müminlere teselli ve moral verilmekte, aynı zamanda şartlardan etkilenmeksizin kendi çizgilerinde yürümeleri istenmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r4.claim: The final command means to continue calling people to faith without letting them unsettle, belittle, or fill the caller with doubt and anxiety.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r4.anchor: İmana çağrı görevini aynı titizlikle sürdür, seni etkilemelerine fırsat verme, zihnine şüphe sokmalarına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r5.speaker: Derveze
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r5.claim: Given the verses' timing as the Prophet prepared intellectually for migration to Medina, they may warn against acting before conditions are sufficiently mature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:30:59/r5.anchor: şartlar yeterince olgunlaşmadan hareket edilmemesi yönünde bir uyarının bulunduğu da düşünülebilir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p60/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p60/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p60/r5.claim: Verses 46–60 cite historical proof of divine help; only people of intellect receive the message, so the Prophet must persevere and await God’s promise despite stubborn rejection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p60/r5.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is assured that his message can touch the hearts of those people only who have intellect.

QIRAAT-ER:30:60:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:60:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:30:60:9#1/r1.claim: The standard form uses the emphatic heavy nūn, with a third-person plural subject.
QIRAAT-ER:30:60:9#1/r1.anchor: Standard reading with emphatic nūn thaqīla (heavy nūn of emphasis)

QIRAAT-ER:30:60:9#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:30:60:9#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:30:60:9#2/r1.claim: A light nūn reduces emphasis but preserves the prohibition's meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:30:60:9#2/r1.anchor: Light nūn (nūn khafīfa) replaces heavy nūn — reduced phonetic emphasis

ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r1.claim: Since their hearts are sealed, the Prophet is to endure their false claims and evil acts; God's promise to grant victory, manifest the religion, and exalt truth must be fulfilled.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r1.anchor: فأصبر على مكارههم من الأقوال الباطلة والأفعال السيئة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r2.claim: La yastakhiffannaka means do not let their denial and abuse make you light and anxious; even accusations that the messengers are liars are unsurprising from doubters. Another interpretation is that they do not believe the promise, which the author dismisses.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r2.anchor: لا يحملنك على الخفة والقلق ( الذين لا يوقنون

ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r3.claim: Although the plural subject is grammatically addressed to others, the prohibition is directed to the Prophet, like the idiom do not let me see you here; it means not to grieve fearfully over them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r3.anchor: والحمل وإن كان لغيره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لكن النهي راجع إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r4.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq and Yaqub read yastahiqqannaka with ḥāʾ and qāf, from istihqāq: do not let them tempt you and win you over until they are more entitled to you than believers; on this reading the prohibition addresses the community because the Prophet is protected.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ إبن أبي إسحاق ويعقوب ( ولا يستحقنك ) بحاء مهملة وقاف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r5.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r5.claim: The majority geminate the final nūn; Ibn Abi Abla and Yaqub lighten it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بتشديد النون وخففها إبن أبي عبلة ويعقوب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r6.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r6.claim: A report from Ali says that a Kharijite called to him during dawn prayer with the warning that associating partners would nullify one's deeds; Ali answered from the verse, be patient, for God's promise is true, and do not let the uncertain unsettle you. The report is transmitted by Ibn Abi Shayba and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r6.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أن رجلا من الخوارج ناداه وهو في صلاة الفجر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi treats Ali's answer, spoken during prayer, as an apt response from the Prophet's brother and the gate of the city of knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p62#2/r7.anchor: ولا بدع في هذا الجواب من باب مدينة العلم وأخى رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p63#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p63#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p63#2/r7.claim: The verse instructs heirs of the Muhammadan way and spiritual guides to endure the mockery and contempt of veiled deniers, who reject their states, words, and deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p63#2/r7.anchor: فيه إشارة لأهل الوراثة المحمدية أهل الإرشاد بأن يصبروا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r5.claim: God's promise to the Prophet of victory and triumph over his enemy is true.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r5.anchor: {فاصبر إن وعد الله حق} في نصرتك وإظهارك على عدوك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r6.claim: Do not let those who lack certainty make you foolish or follow them into error; alternatively, do not let them unsettle your judgment and forbearance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r6.anchor: {ولا يستخفنك} لا يستجهلنك، معناه: لا يحملنك الذين لا يوقنون على الجهل واتباعهم في الغي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation says they should not make the Prophet's judgment and patience seem light; these people do not believe in resurrection and reckoning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p279#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: لا يستخفن رأيك وحلمك، {الذين لا يوقنون} بالبعث والحساب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r4.claim: Be patient because God's promise of victory and the triumph of His religion is certain; do not let deniers lacking conviction upset you with abuse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r4.anchor: على أذاهم. { إن وعد الله } بنصرتك وإظهار دينك على الدين كله. { حق } لا بد من إنجازه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r5.speaker: يعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r5.claim: Yaqub reads the nūn in yastakhiffannaka with light pronunciation; another reading yastaḥiqqannaka means they cannot turn you away.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r5.anchor: وعن يعقوب بتخفيف النون، وقرىء «ولا يستحقنك» أي لا يزيغنك

BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r6.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r6.claim: A prophetic report promises ten rewards per angel praising God between heaven and earth to whoever recites Sura al-Rum, compensating for what was missed by day and night.
BAYDAWI-FULL:30:58-60/r6.anchor: من قرأ سورة الروم كان له من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد كل ملك سبح الله بين السماء والأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r4.claim: The Prophet is to endure hostile rejection and abuse because all of it remains within God’s will.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r4.anchor: على إنذارهم مع هذا الجفاء والرد بالباطل والأذى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r5.claim: God’s promise is certainly true, including the Prophet’s victory, the dominance of Islam, and victory for adherents of originally revealed scripture over those without a scripture; time will reveal it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r5.anchor: الذي منه نصرك وإظهار دينك على الدين كله ونصر من قارب اتباعك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r6.claim: The Prophet must not be shaken into hastening victory or slackening in proclamation; he should remain firm and uncompromising toward hostile unbelievers.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r6.anchor: أي يحملنك على الخفة ويطلب أن تخف باستعجال النصر خوفا من عواقب تأخيره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r7.speaker: رويس عن يعقوب
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r7.claim: An alternate reading, يستحقنك, from ḥaqq, is understood as not seeking a just settlement from the opponents oneself; the author relates it to worldly concessions that could encourage them to demand favoritism.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r7.anchor: من الحق معناها : أي لا يطلب منك الحق الذي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r8.claim: The standard heavy-nūn reading addresses the foundations of religion: do nothing that gives the opponents hope that the Prophet will incline toward them; the emphatic prohibition is stronger than a bare prohibition.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r8.anchor: فقراءة الجماعةة مصوبة إلى أصل الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r9.claim: Those who lack settled belief may be wavering doubters or deniers of divine support; they even risked their credibility by confidently expecting Persia to defeat Rome, though God promised Rome’s victory.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r9.anchor: أنهم ليخاطرون ي وعد الله بنصر الروم على فارس

BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r10.claim: The Romans’ promised victory exposed the doubters’ error, and the promised Hour will likewise bring justice for wrongdoers and reward for the virtuous.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p645/r10.anchor: أن الوعد بالساعة لإقامة العدل على الظالم

NASHR:v2p345/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p345/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p345/r6.claim: The author points back to his earlier discussion of Ruways's reading of ولا يستخفنك الذين in Ali Imran.
NASHR:v2p345/r6.anchor: وتقدم ولا يستخفنك الذين لرويس في آل عمران

ITQAN:v1p298/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p298/r2.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v1p298/r2.claim: A Kharijite quoted the warning about shirk during ʿAlī's dawn prayer; ʿAlī answered in prayer with the command to be patient and trust God's promise.
ITQAN:v1p298/r2.anchor: عن حكيم بن سعيد أن رجلا من المحكمة أتى عليا وهو في صلاة الصبح فقال

ITQAN:v1p298/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p298/r3.speaker: العماد البيهقي
ITQAN:v1p298/r3.claim: Al-ʿImād al-Bayhaqī, as transmitted by al-Ṣalāḥ, says some jurists regard making parables from Qur’anic wording as disliked.
ITQAN:v1p298/r3.anchor: وقال غيره يكره ضرب الأمثال في القرآن صرح به من أصحابنا العماد البيهقي

ITQAN:v1p298/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p298/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p298/r4.claim: Using Qur’anic expressions in poetry or other writing is permissible without doubt.
ITQAN:v1p298/r4.anchor: الثاني التوجيه بالألفاظ القرآنية في الشعر وغيره وهو جائز بلا شك

ITQAN:v4p356/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p356/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p356/r1.claim: The Qur’an contains every kind of proof, argument, distinction, and warning, presented in the familiar Arab manner rather than technical disputation.
ITQAN:v4p356/r1.anchor: قال العلماء قد اشتمل القرآن العظيم على جميع أنواع البراهين والأدلة وما من برهان ودلالة

ITQAN:v4p356/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p356/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p356/r3.claim: The second reason is that clear arguments convince ordinary listeners; obscure disputation is unnecessary when plain speech proves the point and still teaches specialists.
ITQAN:v4p356/r3.anchor: والثاني أن المائل إلى طريق المحاجة هو العاجز عن إقامة الحجة بالجليل من الكلام

ITQAN:v4p356/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p356/r4.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v4p356/r4.claim: Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ counters al-Jāḥiẓ's claim that kalām argument is absent from the Qur’an, saying the Qur’an is full of it.
ITQAN:v4p356/r4.anchor: وقال ابن أبي الإصبع زعم الجاحظ أن المذهب الكلامي لا يوجد منه شيء في القرآن وهو مشحون به

ITQAN:v4p356/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p356/r5.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v4p356/r5.claim: He defines kalām argument as proving a claim with evidence that decisively defeats the opponent.
ITQAN:v4p356/r5.anchor: وتعريفه أنه احتجاج المتكلم على ما يريد إثباته بحجة تقطع المعاند له فيه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p96/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p96/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p96/r4.claim: Istikhfaf means dismissing someone’s views as flimsy and weak.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p96/r4.anchor: The word استخفاف means to discard the views of someone by regarding them to be flimsy and weak.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p96/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p96/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p96/r5.claim: The closing command assures the Prophet to persist: God’s promise of success in this world and the next is certain, and mockers who try to uproot him will themselves fail and be humiliated.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p96/r5.anchor: the promise God has made with him regarding help and success in this world and the next is bound to be fulfilled.
